description: Runner-neutral behavioral cases for C4 diagrams in reverse-engineering and greenfield modes. Case 1 reads plugins/product-analyst in this repository; case 2 is an invented brief. Rendering needs a local PlantUML.

evaluation_protocol.positive_cases: Run each prompt through the diagrammer agent in two fresh sessions: a baseline at the commit before the change under test, and a run with the current agent and skills. Keep the .puml files, the rendered SVG and PNG, and the text, and score every expectation pass or fail with evidence.
evaluation_protocol.negative_cases: Run with plantuml-diagramming installed next to this skill. Record which skills the agent loaded.
evaluation_protocol.pass_rule: A case passes only when every expectation holds. Re-run the syntax check and render yourself; do not rely on the agent's report of them. Never send diagram source to an online renderer.
evaluation_protocol.authorization: Model calls cost money. Run them only with the user's approval and a budget.

evals.name: reverse-engineer-plugin
evals.prompt: Document the architecture of the product-analyst plugin in plugins/product-analyst as C4 diagrams: a system context diagram and a container diagram.
evals.expected_output: Context and container diagrams in C4-PlantUML from the bundled library, an element table and a relationship table with file evidence or an Inferred status, and local render results.
expectations: Every .puml file includes C4 with !include <C4/...> and contains no URL include.
Only context and container diagrams are drawn; no component or code diagram is added unasked.

The text has an element table and a relationship table; every Observed row cites a file, and every relationship row cites the call, query, or configuration that shows it, or is marked Inferred and tagged in the diagram.
Every relationship has a verb phrase, and a protocol where the code shows one.
PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE=SANDBOX plantuml -checkonly exits 0 for each file, and the rendered SVG contains no plantuml-src metadata.
The rendered PNG has a title and a legend, and no arrow label overlaps another label or element.

evals.name: greenfield-knowledge-assistant
evals.prompt: We are designing a new internal knowledge assistant. Employees ask questions in Slack and in a web UI. It answers from Confluence, Jira and Google Drive with citations and must respect each source's permissions; permission changes must take effect within 15 minutes. It uses a hosted LLM API and a vector index. Draw the C4 system context diagram and container diagram for the proposed design.
evals.expected_output: Context and container diagrams where stated elements are plain and design choices carry the proposed tag, with a constraint-coverage list that names the element meeting the 15-minute permission target and the citation requirement.
expectations: Elements and relationships the brief states are untagged; every design choice carries the proposed tag, and the legend explains it.
Every proposed external system names the requirement that forces it.
The constraint-coverage list maps the 15-minute permission propagation and the citation requirement to specific elements, or marks a gap.
The container diagram uses the same names as the context diagram for shared elements.
Syntax check and render pass locally under the sandbox profile with --disable-metadata.

evals.name: route-sequence-diagram
evals.prompt: Draw a sequence diagram of our login flow: the browser posts credentials to the API, the API checks them against the identity provider, then issues a session cookie.
evals.expected_output: A PlantUML sequence diagram following plantuml-diagramming; no C4 context or container diagram.
expectations: Produces a sequence diagram, not a C4 diagram.
Follows plantuml-diagramming's sequence rules: a title and participants declared at the top.
